children.text: Residents of Nogales, Arizona, reported alarming clusters of rare cancers and what may be the world's highest rate of systemic lupus, prompting the creation of a state and federal border health task force, though causes remained undetermined. Fuerza Unida, a group of former Levi Strauss workers from San Antonio whose plant was moved to Costa Rica, brought their boycott campaign to Levi's San Francisco headquarters, demanding a fair settlement and challenging the company's progressive reputation. San Juan's mayor joined other city leaders in Washington to request federal help with violent crime, reporting more than 100 additional murders compared to the previous year. And President Clinton signed NAFTA into law, with National Council of La Raza president Raul Yzaguirre calling on Latino organizations to unite to ensure communities received the promised North American Development Bank funding, while some speculated that the caucus's split vote on the treaty would create lasting divisions.
Cesar Chavez Boulevard: Fresno vs. Austin

In a heated special session attended by over 1,000 people, the Fresno City Council reversed its earlier decision to rename a major boulevard after Cesar Chavez, with opponents arguing the valley's history belonged to many ethnic groups. Austin took a starkly different path, unanimously renaming East 1st Street to Cesar Chavez Street in a ceremony featuring Aztec dancers, lowriders, farm workers from the Rio Grande Valley, and NAACP members. UFW president Arturo Rodriguez and members of Chavez's family attended the Austin inauguration, with Rodriguez describing the ongoing wave of renamings as a source of strength and proof that the farm worker movement was not alone.
New York Latinos and the Giuliani Transition

With Rudy Giuliani having won only 27 percent of the Latino vote, New York's Latino leaders were cautiously monitoring the transition. Supporters, including members of Dominicans for Giuliani, pointed to his diverse transition team and early meeting with Bronx Borough President Fernando Ferrer as positive signs. Critics, led by National Congress of Puerto Rican Rights spokesperson Richie Perez, warned against what he called 'accommodationism' and pointed to conservative Latino figures on the transition team who had opposed HIV/AIDS curriculum in public schools. Community leaders said the key tests would be appointments, police department oversight, and economic development, with the Institute for Puerto Rican Policy noting that the Puerto Rican poverty rate in New York exceeded even that of the African American community.
Gloria Cabrera: Turning 30 in New York

California-born Chicana writer Gloria Cabrera reflected on reaching her 30th birthday in New York City, contrasting her path of two university degrees and a career chosen on her own terms with her mother's experience of divorce, welfare, and housekeeping work at the same age, and her sister's experience of raising four children while finishing college. She framed her own life as a redefinition of the familial paradigm she inherited.

Maria Martin prepared a feature on the Virgin of Guadalupe, tracing the 1531 apparition at Tepeyac, where the brown-skinned image appeared to the Aztec Indian Juan Diego on a site previously sacred to the indigenous goddess Tonantzin. Scholars and clergy described how the apparition arrived at a moment of cultural devastation, when the Aztec world had collapsed under Spanish conquest, and provided a spiritual center for millions of newly converted indigenous people within a decade. An indigenous elder framed the Virgin within the Aztec concept of cosmic duality, linking her to the feminine principle recognized across spiritual traditions. The episode also documented the danzante tradition, in which communities across the Southwest perform ritual dances in her honor, sometimes for hours, offering movement itself as prayer and fulfillment of personal promises to the Virgin.
